**University Emblem**

**Plan of Studies**  
**Program Code:** QF-AQAC-02.03  
**Edition:** 210   

**Courses Overview:**

1. **0441737 Mukhtalaf Al-Hadith (3 credit Hours)**  
   This course deals with the meaning of Mukhtalaf al-Hadith (what appears contradicted superficially) its reasons, methods of clarifying this obscurity, the development of this science, and its most important sources. The course will concentrate also on an applied study to certain obscure Hadiths in details.

2. **0431738 ‘Ilal al-Hadith (3 credit Hours)**  
   This course deals with the science of ‘Ilal (the unclear hidden problematic defects of the narration) by giving its definition, history, development, bases, procedures of knowing the ‘Ilah, and the main sources of this science.

3. **0431742 Language in Hadith (3 credit Hours)**  
   This course deals in depth with the prophetic sayings from a linguistic viewpoint by dealing with the ancient authentic linguistic resources which have been concerned in this issue.

4. **0441743 Scientific Inimitability in the Qur’an and Sunnah (3 credit Hours)**  
   This course investigates and discusses the scientific facts in which Qur’an and Sunnah have pointed out to, long time ago in different scientific areas. It is highly recommended in this course that the students should study in the introduction the standpoint of contemporary scholars towards this issue. In specific, the student should have a look at the production of the “specialized council in scientific inimitability of the Qur’an and Sunnah”.

5. **0441744 Thematic Hadith (3 credit Hours)**  
   This course deals with certain subjects by collecting Hadith concerning them, then to edit these Hadiths by giving their sources and degrees (according to Hadith sciences), then to arrange these Hadiths in the same subject, and finally to give the conclusion to each Hadith subject.

6. **0401746 The Sunnah in Contemporary Studies (3 credit Hours)**  
   This course deals with the Scholars’ efforts and manners in all Hadith sources and encyclopedias, and the development of encyclopedically classification until modern encyclopedias, which use computer systems.
